content: The Guideline Development Group (GDG) included a diverse range of members, representing future users of the guidelines and individuals affected by the recommendations, including patients. Prior to the GDG meeting held at the WHO headquarters in Geneva, Switzerland, from July 11 to 13, 2016, specific members were assigned to review the evidence for each PICO (Population, Intervention, Comparator, Outcome) question. These members presented their perspectives on the implications of the findings during the meeting. Evidence profiles and drafts of review reports were shared with GDG members before the meeting. During the meeting and in the subsequent weeks, additional analyses were provided to the group upon request. The GDG discussed the GRADE (Grading of Recommendations, Assessment, Development, and Evaluation) evidence profiles before formulating recommendations. The group utilized Evidence-to-Decision tables via the GRADEpro interface to document the content of their discussions. During the July 2016 meeting, the GDG formulated the initial draft of the recommendations based on their assessment of the evidence. They deliberated on the proposed wording of the recommendations and the strength of each recommendation (strong or conditional). This process considered not only the quality and nature of the evidence but also the balance between benefits and harms, patient values and preferences, resource implications, equity and human rights, acceptability, and feasibility. For the question regarding the use of the Category II regimen for treating previously treated tuberculosis (TB), the evidence generated using the GRADE approach was insufficient for the GDG to make a recommendation. Instead, a good practice statement approach was deemed more appropriate and was used to formulate the recommendation. All decisions on the recommendations, including their strength and any conditions attached, were reached through discussion and consensus. The Chair facilitated these discussions to achieve consensus, eliminating the need for voting on any recommendations. After the GDG meeting, an additional analysis was conducted to address a gap in information identified in PICO question 10, which focused on treatment adherence interventions. This additional evidence led to a slight revision of two recommendations related to treatment supervision options. All evidence and revised recommendations were shared with GDG members for review and endorsement. The external review process involved the External Review Group, which consisted of experts and end-users from national programs, technical agencies, and WHO regional offices. These individuals provided their feedback on the completed draft guidelines after incorporating comments from GDG members. The guidelines are published on the WHO Global TB Programme (WHO/GTB) website and are freely available for download in PDF and other electronic formats. A print version of the main text was scheduled for release in early 2017 and distributed widely to WHO regional and country offices, as well as national TB programs. The document is available in six languages: Arabic, Chinese, English, French, Russian, and Spanish. The recommendations will also be published in peer-reviewed journals to enhance the dissemination of the main messages. Updates to policy guidance will be reflected in the implementation guidance on TB management and the revised WHO implementation handbook on the programmatic management of drug-resistant TB. WHO will collaborate with its regional and country offices, technical and funding agencies, and partners to ensure widespread communication of the updated guidance through technical meetings and training activities. WHO will work with technical partners to support national TB programs in adopting the new recommendations into national TB policies and guidelines. The implementation of the recommendations by countries or end-users will be evaluated by WHO/GTB and partners several years after publication. WHO/GTB will also review and update the guidelines approximately 4–5 years after publication, or earlier if new evidence becomes available. These updates will be reflected in the implementation guidance documents.
